rubrics.name: Findable
rubrics.rationale: estimate: PID present (scheme: DOI); PID resolved; deposited in a sustainable repository (Zenodo); that the PID resolves to a specific VERSION of the dataset is not verified — confirm before accepting (the gate requires a 2 here)

rubrics.name: Accessible
rubrics.rationale: estimate: metadata fetchable via PID lookup; standard vocabularies referenced: MeSH

rubrics.name: Interoperable
rubrics.rationale: estimate: metadata is JSON-LD; standard vocabularies referenced: MeSH

rubrics.name: Reusable
rubrics.rationale: estimate: machine-readable license linked in the metadata (Apache-2.0); no AI/ML prohibition language found in license or use terms

rubrics.name: Transparent
rubrics.rationale: estimate: 6 datasets carry provenance links; ground-truth elements missing: samples, instruments

rubrics.name: Traceable
rubrics.rationale: estimate: 5 machine-readable transformation steps; every computation links its software; completeness of the provenance record (or disclosure of known gaps) is asserted, not verified; final score is capped at 1.a's score (rule 1.b ≤ 1.a)
rubrics.capped_by: dependency rule 1.b ≤ 1.a: score lowered from 2 to 1

rubrics.name: Interpretable
rubrics.rationale: estimate: 1 of 5 archived with a PID; 4 on mutable code hosting only

rubrics.name: Key actors identified
rubrics.rationale: estimate: 1 of 2 authors carry a PID; 1 named in free text only

rubrics.name: Semantics
rubrics.rationale: estimate: abstract present (695 chars — length-checked only, not read for substance); 12 keywords; 4 controlled-vocabulary terms

rubrics.name: Statistics
rubrics.rationale: estimate: 6 entities carry a summary-statistics link; missing-data statement present (its consistency and domain-appropriateness are asserted, not verified against the files)

rubrics.name: Standards
rubrics.rationale: estimate: 1 schema entities; standard vocabulary bindings populated: Croissant, Wikidata

rubrics.name: Potential Sources of Bias
rubrics.rationale: judged: rai:dataBiases names specific sources (single target host, benign baseline from the author's personal academic/Linux infrastructure, under-representation of enterprise SOC telemetry), and rai:dataLimitations adds processing assumptions (24.2% eBPF downsampling losing temporal correlation, known-TTP-only attacks, simulated defense state). Missingness is measured and explained per column (e.g. src_ip NULL on 93.5% because eBPF/syslog events have no client address), and the benign-vs-malicious balance is quantified (20,901,688 vs 609,520 rows).

rubrics.name: Data quality
rubrics.rationale: judged: Domain-specific QC is applied and described concretely: nine automated validation checks on every composed stream (label consistency, per-attack-type raw-line regex spot checks, campaign containment, distribution vs composition weights, temporal monotonicity, session label coherence) plus signature-based MaliciousFilter cleaning of the benign baseline. This is appropriate for labeled security-log data; the main weakness is that no link to the validation protocol/software is given in the collection/processing descriptions.

rubrics.name: Data documentation template
rubrics.rationale: estimate: human-readable datasheet linked; 8 of 9 machine-readable sections populated (presence-checked only — whether coverage is substantive is a human read)

rubrics.name: Fit for purpose
rubrics.rationale: estimate: appropriate and inappropriate uses both stated; 1 prior publications linked

rubrics.name: Verifiable
rubrics.rationale: estimate: checksums on all 6 datasets and software (embargoed excluded)

rubrics.name: Ethically acquired
rubrics.rationale: judged: Acquisition is described with source and a legitimacy statement (author-operated servers, isolated lab VM, 'no third-party infrastructure was probed'). However, there is no ethics review, no human-subjects determination or exemption basis, and no consent/waiver basis for retaining 11,413 public visitor IPs; the 'management plan' is a versioning/issue-tracker note, not a DMP/DMSP.

rubrics.name: Ethically managed
rubrics.rationale: judged: Sensitivity is declared (HL7 confidentiality 'moderate') and the personal-information statement is candid: hostnames/addresses are mapped to a synthetic identity, but 860,529 benign rows retain one of 11,413 public IPv4 addresses. No justification is given for retaining these identifiers, no PIA or equivalent risk assessment, and no re-identification reassessment plan; the management plan only covers versioning.

rubrics.name: Ethically Disseminated
rubrics.rationale: judged: The data is openly released under Apache-2.0 (a software license) with intended research uses listed, but no prohibited uses, no conditionsOfAccess/DUA, and no contact are given. Ethical use boundaries are therefore vague, notably for data that retains third-party public IPs; this sits at 1 rather than 0 only because a license and permitted-use statement exist.

rubrics.name: Secure
rubrics.rationale: estimate: confidentiality level is an HL7 v3-Confidentiality code ('M'); whether the declared level is actually ENFORCED (the 0-rule) is not verified — score 0 if controlled data is retrievable without authorization or authorized users are blocked

rubrics.name: Persistent
rubrics.rationale: estimate: PID present (scheme: DOI); recognized archive(s): Zenodo; an explicit retention commitment is assumed for recognized repositories, not verified; note the criterion covers RAW/unprocessed data — confirm the raw data itself is what's archived

rubrics.name: Domain-appropriate
rubrics.rationale: judged: Data is deposited in Zenodo (recognized generalist repository with DOIs) and mirrored on HuggingFace. Cybersecurity log/benchmark data has no widely recognized sustainable specialist repository, so a generalist repository satisfies the criterion.

rubrics.name: Well-governed
rubrics.rationale: judged: rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan is present and links a resolving issue tracker, describing DOI versioning (concept DOI plus frozen v4.1) and HF mirror sync. It does not address long-term stewardship, maintenance commitments/duration, responsible party, or how policy/terms changes are handled; no governance committee or responsible party is named.

rubrics.name: Associated
rubrics.rationale: estimate: components associated machine-readably in the archived metadata record (hasPart / distribution + provenance links); accessibility of every component not verified — downgrade if pieces are missing

rubrics.name: Standardized
rubrics.rationale: estimate: declared standards: Croissant, Dublin Core, W3C PROV-O, schema.org; deterministic validator known: Croissant — mlcroissant validator; JSON Schema — any JSON Schema validator (e.g. python-jsonschema); PROV-O — PROV-CONSTRAINTS validation (ProvToolbox `provconvert -validate`); populated vocabulary bindings present (final score is capped at 2.c's score — rule 6.a ≤ 2.c)

rubrics.name: Computationally accessible
rubrics.rationale: judged: All 6 distributions have direct HTTPS contentUrls on Zenodo and HuggingFace, both reachable and both backed by formally documented public APIs (Zenodo REST API, HF Hub/datasets API), with open access requiring no human intervention. Access instructions (conditionsOfAccess) are absent, but none are needed for open data.

rubrics.name: Portable
rubrics.rationale: judged: The data is 6 Zstandard-compressed files in open formats with no proprietary formats, so it requires no specialized compute environment to use. The software is pip-installable (security-gym 0.4.2 on PyPI with pyproject.toml), though no container or conda environment and no hardware requirements are declared (0/4 computations with a container).

rubrics.name: Contextualized
rubrics.rationale: estimate: machine-readable example dataset provided; withheld/preprocessing information described; splits N/A unless the dataset should define them — reviewer to confirm
